title: Air fryers rolled to a later vessel
brief: German B2B customers are missing deliveries of SKU F-900 (air fryer) this week. Find the root cause and an action plan.

evidence.content: A dock strike at the port of Hamburg has delayed many vessels since 8 Nov.
F-900 on-hand at Duisburg is 120 units against 1,400 units of open B2B orders. The next inbound, PO 5520 (2,000 units), is expected 12 Nov.
Production of PO 5520 was completed on 25 Oct.
PO 5520 is booked on vessel MAERSK ELBA, Ningbo -> Rotterdam, then rail to Duisburg; ETA Duisburg 12 Nov.
We missed the 27 Oct cut-off for MAERSK ELBA: the export carton labels failed your retailer's labelling compliance check and had to be reprinted. The cargo was rolled to the next sailing.
Correction: our booking system was not updated after the roll. PO 5520 is now on MSC ANNA, departing Ningbo 10 Nov, ETA Rotterdam 12 Dec.
German B2B demand for F-900 is in line with forecast.

answer_key.root_cause: PO 5520 missed its vessel cut-off because the supplier's carton labels failed retailer compliance and had to be reprinted; the cargo was rolled to a sailing arriving about a month later, while the booking system still showed the old ETA. The Hamburg strike is unrelated (the cargo routes via Rotterdam).

remediation_rubric.criterion: Bridge the ~1 month gap: air-freight part of the volume or reallocate from other EU DCs
Allocate available stock across B2B customers and communicate revised dates
Check labelling compliance with the supplier before cut-off
Fix ETA visibility: forwarder must update bookings after a roll
Explicitly rules out the Hamburg strike

answer_key.notes: E1 is a tempting distractor; E4 is stale and corrected by E6 in round 3.

registry.mechanism_opportunities: V3: E6 corrects E4; an alert can stop the team relying on the 12 Nov ETA. D0 may propagate the stale ETA.
registry.expected_timing: Plausible but wrong answers possible in round 2; full answer needs E6 (round 3).
registry.favoritism_notes: Could favour V3 (correction handling). Balanced by HO-06 and HO-02, where alerts are useless.
